title: [ci] SEVEN more combined `actions/cache` saves carry the unbounded-save exposure #6577 measured — across five workflows, not just ci.yml
body:
Filed unassigned by the `domain:devx @ objectui` PM seat. This is the generalisation question that #6577's implementer **escalated rather than rode along** — its PR #7047 says, correctly, *"generalising was not in the charter; that is a question for the PM, not a rider on this PR."*

⚠️ **This body was corrected after filing — the original scoped the population to `ci.yml` and undercounted it by more than 3x.** See the correction comment below; the error and its cause are recorded rather than quietly overwritten.

Attribution as prose, because the footer block is stripped from issue bodies written through this path (#6970): generated by Claude Code, PM session `86aefd79-6ef3-5a63-98f9-701da03c59ab`.

## The mechanism is no longer hypothetical

#6577 measured it once and PR #7047 established the whole shape of it:

- `actions/cache@v6` declares `post: 'dist/save/index.js'` in its own `action.yml`. The save is a step the **runner generates** at job end — **no workflow syntax can attach `timeout-minutes` or `continue-on-error` to it.**
- So an unbounded save can run its job into the job ceiling. The job goes `cancelled`.
- **The merge queue cannot tell `cancelled` from `failure`** ⇒ a pull request whose gate had already reported success is ejected, and the shared serial queue is head-of-line blocked for the whole ceiling first.
- Measured on the incident: a healthy save of that cache is **1 second**; the stalled one ran **789 seconds**.

⇒ The exposure is a property of *using the combined action in a job with a ceiling*, not a property of the `type-check` job.

## The real population — measured on `main` = `50afa361d`

Read directly across **all 31 workflow files** (control: 31 files enumerated, non-zero). **Eight combined uses in five workflows**, and a second query confirms **zero** already use the split `actions/cache/restore` + `actions/cache/save` form:

| workflow | line | status |
|:--|--:|:--|
| `ci.yml` — `type-check`, ceiling 20 min | 425 | ⏳ fixed by PR #7047 (in flight) |
| `ci.yml` — `e2e`, **Playwright browsers (~269 MB)**, ceiling 30 min | 1069 | ⛔ exposed |
| `ci.yml` — `docs`, ceiling 15 min | 1234 | ⛔ exposed |
| `lint.yml` | 244 | ⛔ exposed |
| `live-e2e.yml` | 98 | ⛔ exposed |
| `live-e2e.yml` | 163 | ⛔ exposed |
| `performance-budget.yml` | 138 | ⛔ exposed |
| `changeset-release.yml` | 576 | ⛔ exposed |

⇒ **Seven remain exposed after #7047 lands, not two.**

### ⭐ Two refinements, both cutting toward acting

1. **The `e2e` cache is not a turbo cache — it is Playwright browser binaries, ~269 MB.** Upload duration scales with size, so on the one axis that drives this defect `e2e` is the **most** exposed, not the least.
2. **`docs` has the tightest ceiling of the ci.yml three (15 min)** ⇒ least headroom between a stalled save and a `cancelled` check.

⚠️ Neither is a measurement of a hang. They are reasons the exposure is not obviously smaller elsewhere.

## ⛔ What this card does NOT claim

- ⛔ **No second occurrence has been observed.** #6577 is n=1 and **stays** n=1; PR #7047 says so explicitly and this card does not upgrade it.
- ⛔ **Not corroborated by objectui#7010.** Those three merge-queue wedges are a **different shape**: zero `merge_group` runs were ever dispatched, versus a run that existed with one job cancelled. Do not cite #7010 here — conflating them manufactures a pattern out of two unrelated faults.
- ⛔ Not a claim that any of the seven has ever hung. **This is exposure, not a defect.**
- ⚠️ **The seven are not equally exposed and this card has not ranked them.** Only `ci.yml`'s three were examined for ceiling and cache content; the four in `lint.yml` / `live-e2e.yml` / `performance-budget.yml` / `changeset-release.yml` are listed from a line-level grep only. **Whoever takes this re-derives each one.**

## The actual decision

**Is a proven, mechanical fix worth applying pre-emptively to seven more sites, or does each wait for its own occurrence?**

| act now | wait |
|:--|:--|
| The fix is **already derived and pinned** — PR #7047 did the hard part (that `timeout-minutes` cannot reach a generated post step, and that `restore@v6` + `save@v6` is the route `actions/cache`'s own `save-always` deprecation text points at). Applying it is mechanical. | ⛔ No measurement on any of the seven. A CI change with no observed defect behind it is speculative work across five high-blast-radius files. |
| The cost is paid **by every lane**, not the unlucky PR: the queue is one shared serial resource. | The caches differ from the measured one, so #7047's `timeout-minutes: 5` is **not** transferable without re-deriving each site's healthy save duration. |
| ⭐ Seven sites is no longer "an edge case on one job" — it is **the repo's default spelling for caching**, so the exposure is structural rather than incidental. | ⚠️ Seven sites is also seven chances to get a bound wrong, and a bound set below a cache's honest upload time converts a working save into a permanently skipped one. |

⇒ ⭐ **Whoever takes this must not copy `timeout-minutes: 5` across.** That number was sized at **300x the measured 1-second healthy save** for *that* cache. A ~269 MB Playwright cache legitimately takes far longer. **Measure each site's healthy save from the Actions API first; the bound is derived, never inherited.** ⇒ Consider splitting into per-workflow PRs rather than one sweep, so each bound carries its own measurement.

## Fences for whoever takes it

- ⛔ **Do not raise any job's `timeout-minutes`.** Same reason as #6577: a larger ceiling buys a longer hang and still ends in `cancelled`.
- ⛔ **Do not change any verdict-bearing step.** PR #7047 shipped a parser that compares command-bearing steps per job between two revisions **with a control proving it non-vacuous** — reuse it, and paste its output.
- ⛔ **Prove each pin has teeth by ablation**: fold the split back, drop `continue-on-error`, hoist the save above the checking steps. Prove each mutation on disk, then prove the restore by **blob hash**. ⚠️ #7047 recorded a live trap worth inheriting: its first ablation anchor was the phrase `continue-on-error: true`, which also appears in the *comment* the change adds, so the on-disk count could never reach 0 and the leg was a silent no-op — **caught only because its own on-disk check rejected it**. Anchor to the YAML key at its exact indent.
- ⭐ Carry the ordering sentence into each comment, as #7047 did: *the verdict is recorded by the checking steps; everything after them is bookkeeping, and bookkeeping must never discard an answer the gate already produced.*

## Related

- **#6577** / PR **#7047** — the measurement, the mechanism, and the fix this would generalise.
- **#5304** — this repo's `apt-get` precedent already in `ci.yml`: an unbounded network call whose only backstop was the job ceiling.
- **#7010** — ⛔ different shape, listed only so the next reader does not re-link them.
